title: Meshy Just Released New PBR Textures and they're honestly Next Level
author: Axinovium
selftext: Can't wait to see how people use them in their game environments. Anyone here tried Meshy AI yet?

comments.author: UAAgency
comments.body: wow pretty cool ngl, they look good, but how do you get the materials?

replies.author: dragonboltz
replies.body:
Super easy! Just select generate PBR maps when generating models with Meshy, and the PBR textures are automatically included in the download. Then you can just create your materials in unity, blender or unreal the normal way with them. 

https://preview.redd.it/p75r869nrahf1.png?width=595&format=png&auto=webp&s=943f49251267ef7348baf050816ce1c4060ab068

comments.author: ai_art_is_art
comments.body: Will we even need this if world models like Google Genie take over?

replies.author: Signal-Lake-1385
replies.body: I think so - keeping track of state, staying coherent and having rules that are consistent seems like a really big challenge. There are so many specific rules that make up a game, I think if ai can dynamically create coherent, full games on its own and on the fly - then I think at that point there’s nothing it can’t do.

replies.author: No_Surround_4662
replies.body:
Yes. 

Procedurally generated and AI generated games are a gimmick and don't lead to enjoyable or sharable player experiences. People will still prefer pre-generated visuals and stories rather than a completely AI generated video game. Playing these games will look visually impressive, but unless it has predetermined structure it'll be like throwing a pebble in the ocean.

replies.author: ai_art_is_art
replies.body:
Minecraft is the biggest game in the world and it flies in the face of everything you've just said.

\> Interesting thing about Starbound -they spent ages trying to create a procedurally generative monster and biome system and scrapped most of it when they found procedurally generated content didn't actually do much for the gameplay.

A small number of engineers using hand-written algorithms. UGC GenAI would topple this problem in a day. 

\> the user experience has to be carefully tailored

And why wouldn't a world simulator come with a world builder? The input right now is an image or text prompt, but I imagine we'll be getting lots of tools.

replies.author: No_Surround_4662
replies.body:
>Minecraft is the biggest game in the world and it flies in the face of everything you've just said.

Minecraft is procedurally generated, all the items, players, enemies, NPCs, objectives are not procedurally generated, it's exactly the point I'm making.

>A small number of engineers using hand-written algorithms. UGC GenAI would topple this problem in a day.

UGC doesn't exist, and no one knows if it will ever exist. I could say the same thing about using magic to make a game.

>And why wouldn't a world simulator come with a world builder? The input right now is an image or text prompt, but I imagine we'll be getting lots of tools.

Yes, it probably will do. I'm talking about user experience, building games cannot be done purely with AI in the way you think Google Genie will make them.
